instruction: Heartbeat duty: prepare this week's material, one step per sub-agent, all of it held for the CEO's review in the marketing room (nothing is posted). First read .benzene/material/experience/analytics-report.md and .benzene/material/marketing/profile.md. Then: the blog writer one new article in .benzene/material/marketing/articles/; the newsletter agent this ISO week's issue in .benzene/material/marketing/newsletter/ if it is missing; LinkedIn one terminology post, a document carousel (a deck in .benzene/material/marketing/slides/) when fewer than two decks are dated this week; X one thread on the same campaign; Instagram one carousel; Facebook the twin of the newest Instagram campaign; ad boosts a proposal only when a post's engagement is at least twice the channel's median, otherwise nothing. Every post keeps its showcase_url with UTM tags. If the campaign needs product work, end with one line 'SUGGEST COO: <the product work>'.
output:
I wrote `.benzene/material/marketing/articles/skeleton-cls-gate.md` — a new article dated 2026-10-15 (inside ISO week 2026-W42, the week the cadence check flagged as short).

**Claim:** A skeleton that reuses its real row's own CSS class — not a hand-tuned pixel height — is the only version that keeps Cumulative Layout Shift at zero after the row's CSS changes, and a 12-line `PerformanceObserver` script proves that instead of an eyeballed review.

What the file contains:
- Front matter with all required fields: `title`, `date` (2026-10-15), `description` (≤160 chars), `tags: [skeleton, rwd]` (2 tags, from `docs/_data/topics/ui.csv`), `canonical_url` at `elegantfrontend.training/blog/skeleton-cls-gate.html`, `ai_assistance: assisted`, `related_practice: [skeleton-list]` (a real slug from `docs/_data/questions.yml`), and a `syndication` block for devto/hashnode/medium each carrying that same canonical URL.
- Body (~1,050 words) that discloses AI assistance and human review in the first two paragraphs, builds on the `ui-skeleton` skill's "Match Final Layout" principle and the `skeleton-list` practice question's own two solutions (shared-class skeleton vs. real-row-with-placeholder-data), then goes further by introducing a `PerformanceObserver(['layout-shift'])` gate the skill/practice doc doesn't show.
- Two runnable fenced code examples: the shared-class `UserCardSkeleton.jsx` (sourced from the practice doc) and a new `cls-gate.js` snippet computing total layout-shift value across a load transition.
- One original inline `<svg>` figure (`viewBox`, `role="img"`, `<title>`) in the Elegant palette (`#fe854c`, `#155799`, `#202028`, `#fff7f2`) contrasting a spinner's layout jump against the shared-class skeleton's stable box.
- A closing CTA linking to the real practice page `https://elegantfrontend.training/practice/skeleton-list.html`.

This brings the count of articles dated in 2026-W42 from 1 to 2; at least one more article dated in that same week is still needed elsewhere to clear the blog-cadence bar of ≥3/week.
